name.en: Fake police “undercover operation”: withdraw cash for a courier

how.en: Someone calls from an unknown number claiming to be a police officer and gives details to “prove” it. They say they are running an undercover operation into fake bank notes and ask you to withdraw money as evidence, with a script for answering the bank’s questions. They ask for serial numbers, give you a fake number for an insurance claim, and send a courier to your home to collect the cash. Older people are being targeted.

text.en: A caller claims to be a police officer and gives details to prove it.
They say there is an undercover operation into fake bank notes.
They ask you to withdraw cash and give you a script for the bank.
A courier comes to your home to collect the money.

Good afternoon, this is Constable Reid. We are running an undercover operation into counterfeit notes coming from your bank. We need you to withdraw $8,000 for evidence. If the teller asks, just say it is for home renovations.

en: police asked me to withdraw cash
police gave me a script for the bank
A police officer asking you to withdraw or hand over money. Police never do this.
A script for what to tell the bank.
A courier coming to collect cash.
Hang up. To check an officer, ask for their full details and call 105.
Tell your bank if anyone asks you to withdraw cash for an investigation.
Warn older family and friends about this scam.

sources.title: Police impersonator scammers targeting members of the Western Bay of Plenty community
